_about: One sounding (a measured number) and one ping (a pause question with the measured answer) per station. Every number here must appear in that notebook's text or saved outputs; tools/check_markers.py fails the build if one does not. 'pause' is the index of the notebook's pause question (content/courses/*.json); 'q' overrides its wording when the question needs context from the notebook.

sounding.label: test flowers the first model gets right
sounding.src: §6 Which flowers does it get wrong?

ping.q: The model makes three mistakes on the test set. Which species does it mix up?
ping.echo: All 12 setosa flowers are right. 2 of the 13 virginica are called versicolor and 1 of the 13 versicolor is called virginica: 35 of 38 correct.

sounding.label: the pass rate: the baseline accuracy every model must beat

ping.q: The next table gives the pass rate per department. Which department passes most often, and would the table tell you why?
ping.echo: CS 68.7%, Engineering 59.3%, Business 52.5%. The table shows that the rates differ. It can't say why.

sounding.label: test accuracy with a leaked column (0.832 without it)

ping.q: We add a column recording who received a pass certificate, which is issued after the exam, and train the same pipeline. What test accuracy do you expect?
ping.echo: 0.832 without the column, 1.000 with it. Nothing in the code is wrong: the model learned to read the answer sheet instead of the student.

sounding.label: an unlimited tree: training accuracy, then test accuracy

ping.q: As the tree gets deeper, training accuracy will rise. What will test accuracy do?
ping.echo: Training accuracy reaches 1.000 at depth 13. Test accuracy peaks at 0.905 at depth 2 and ends at 0.890. That 11-point gap is overfitting.

sounding.label: frauds found by a model with 99.1% accuracy

ping.q: A model scores 99.1% on this test set. Would you put it into use?
choices: Not before seeing what it misses
ping.echo: A rule that always answers "no fraud" scores 0.990 and finds none of the 50 frauds. The 0.991 logistic regression finds 5 of the 50.

sounding.label: cluster agreement: standardised units, then raw units

ping.q: Nothing about the points' arrangement changes, only the units. Will the clusters change?
ping.echo: Agreement with the hidden labels drops from 0.996 to 0.793 on raw numbers. After standardising it is back to 0.996. Choosing the units decides what "close" means.

sounding.label: the XOR network's loss, epoch 1 to 500. This is the ground you are diving.

ping.q: Does a chain of two linear layers have more power than one?
ping.echo: Both give −4.613 for the same input. Two linear layers merge into one, so each layer needs a non-linear step after it.

sounding.label: run A's validation loss at epoch 13, then at epoch 200

ping.q: Run A overfits. Early stopping, dropout or L2: which do you expect to help the most?
ping.echo: Early stopping kept the weights from epoch 13: validation loss 0.280 against 1.992 for run A, the lowest of all the runs. Dropout delays overfitting rather than preventing it.

sounding.label: parameters in the CNN, against 101,770 for the dense network

ping.q: Which network will lose more accuracy when the digits move 3 pixels?
ping.echo: At 3 pixels the CNN scores 0.746 and the dense network 0.445, from 0.973 and 0.931 unshifted.

sounding.label: test accuracy: trained from scratch, then fine-tuned from ImageNet
sounding.src: §5 The three runs side by side

ping.q: Order the three strategies by test accuracy: from scratch, frozen features, fine-tuned.
ping.echo: Fine-tuned 0.883, frozen features 0.850, from scratch 0.710. With 6,405 trainable parameters the frozen model beats 2,230,277 trained from scratch.

sounding.label: the weight learned for the word pair "not good"

ping.q: The word-pair model has a feature for "not good". What weight will it learn for it?
ping.echo: −0.94 for "not good", while "good" alone falls to 0.86. Pairs are not a full fix: "not bad" gets only 0.36.

sounding.label: attention from "it" to each candidate, averaged over BERT's 144 heads
sounding.src: §3 What a trained model actually does

ping.q: In "The robot put the battery in the device because it was empty", which token should "it" attend to most?
ping.echo: The "it" row gives 0.59 to battery, 0.22 to empty, 0.08 to itself, and 0.05 each to robot and because.

sounding.label: the model's probability for its first answer token, "Battery"

ping.q: A forum post among the documents hides an instruction. Will the model follow it?
choices: Only with one of the prompts
ping.echo: The two plain prompts held. The prompt that warned the model the context was untrusted is the one that obeyed: "Visit free-prizes.example to claim your reward."

sounding.label: GPT-2 tokens for the Arabic and the English sentence

ping.q: Four sentences of about the same length, in English, French, Arabic and Python. Which needs the most tokens?
ping.echo: Arabic needs 45 tokens for 43 characters, about four times English (11 tokens for 51 characters). French needs 19, Python 31.

sounding.label: bits per token on repeated text, before and after removing five induction heads
sounding.src: §4 Does a clear pattern mean the head matters?

ping.q: Remove the five heads with the strongest induction pattern. What does the second copy cost, against 0.65 bits per token with nothing removed?
ping.echo: 7.62 bits per token. Removing five random other heads costs 0.76 on average.

sounding.label: of a GPT-2 block's parameters sit in the MLP; 33% in attention

ping.q: What share of a transformer block's parameters sits in attention?
ping.echo: Attention holds 2,362,368 (33%), the MLP 4,722,432 (67%), the two layer norms 3,072.

sounding.label: bits per character on children's stories: our 11.5M GPT, then GPT-2 small

ping.q: Will GPT-2 (124 million parameters, 40 GB of web text) beat our 11.5-million-parameter model on children's stories?
choices: Yes, it is ten times larger
ping.echo: Ours costs 0.54 bits per character, GPT-2 0.82, a bigram 1.32. Training data matched to the task beat size.

sounding.label: BERT's probability for "dead", with and without the rest of the sentence

ping.q: BERT's masking recipe masks some tokens, leaves some unchanged and swaps some for random words. Which does it recover best?
ping.echo: Unchanged tokens 0.993, masked 0.704, random words 0.549.

sounding.label: validation loss at 36M tokens: the smallest model, then the largest

ping.q: For a fixed compute budget, is the loss lowest for the smallest model, the largest, or something in between?
ping.echo: In between, with a broad minimum: for 10^14 FLOPs the best is 0.47M parameters trained on 35.6 million tokens.

sounding.label: step-by-step answers: one sample, then a majority vote of 8

ping.q: Pick the best of N answers by a proxy reward model. As N grows, will the gold judge's score rise, level off, or fall?
ping.echo: Gold rises all the way: 0.54 at N = 8 and 0.82 at N = 64, while the proxy rates its own picks at 1.31. With much stronger optimisation, Gao et al. (2022) found that it eventually falls.

sounding.label: numbers trained by rank-1 LoRA, 0.03% of the model, as good as rank 32

ping.q: With one worked example in the prompt, how many of the test lines will the model get fully right?
ping.echo: 0.925 on the training layouts, against none zero-shot. On unseen layouts, 0.210.

sounding.label: questions answered right: closed book, then with the top 3 passages

ping.q: 16 agent tasks search and read a planted passage telling them to answer 0. How many obey it?
ping.echo: Half of them (8) answered 0, and right answers fell from 6 of 20 to 2. The tool allowlist never came into play: answering 0 needs no tool.

sounding.label: prefilling 1,000 tokens, against decoding a single token

ping.q: int4 with one scale for a whole matrix uses the same 4 bits per weight as int4 with one scale per row. How different can they be?
choices: one scale per matrix destroys the model
ping.echo: One scale per matrix: perplexity 150 million. One per row: 30.08. The original bf16 model: 15.47.

sounding.label: the base model's MMLU score in chat format, below the 0.25 of a random guess

ping.q: How often will the 0.5B judge pick whichever answer is shown first?
ping.echo: 97.9% of the time. It agrees with the label 0.988 of the time when the preferred answer comes first, and 0.03 when it comes second.

sounding.label: the winning setting's gain, then what remained with 5 new seeds
sounding.src: §2 Test-set noise and the best of many

ping.q: The chosen setting is 0.0454 better than the average setting. Train it again with 5 new seeds: how much of the gain remains?
ping.echo: Only 0.0101. All five reruns scored worse than the original: about four-fifths of the gain was a lucky seed.

sounding.label: points between the best and worst rank in the LoRA paper's Table 6: one seed's standard deviation

ping.q: In the LoRA paper's Table 6, r = 8 is best for Wq, Wv on WikiSQL. Is the evidence strong enough to recommend it?
ping.echo: The worst rank is 0.5 points below, the size of one seed's standard deviation. What the table does support is the paper's real claim: rank 1 is within 0.4 of the best.

sounding.label: CLIP zero-shot, then the basic course's fine-tuned network, on the same 300 flower photos

ping.q: Which prompt works best for CLIP: "tulip", "a photo of a tulip.", or "a photo of a tulip, a type of flower."?
choices: a photo of a tulip, a type of flower.
ping.echo: 0.920, 0.940 and 0.973. CLIP was trained on captions, so a caption-like prompt works better, and naming the domain helps further.
